I use iPhone Mirroring every day to quickly access my iPhone directly on my Mac, and this year the feature is getting even better. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate both launched this month, bringing three important updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's a look at all the new features.

macOS 27: What's New with iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window using any iOS 27-compatible app. For now, this only applies to Apple's native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later, the range of resizable apps will expand rapidly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. The changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27...

expected to launch later this year.

There are several other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Control Center Access
  • DRM Video Support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or through the View menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos on your Mac through iPhone Mirroring. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would only display a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was enabled.

macOS 27 also gives iPhone Mirroring a new app icon, matching several other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried them in the public beta? Let us know in the comments.
